name: CUTDOWN
summary: Punch in/out on a folder of footage and let the lane render the cuts.
_calls_note: What this app CALLS — a different fact from what a provider ANSWERS. It was `verbs`, a flat list doing double duty: authored by the app to mean a dependency, consumed by the composer as provider routing. Every one is required: cutdown without its verbs is a picture of a video editor.

requires._filters_note: REQUIRED vs PREFERRED, and the split is the point. scale/concat are load-bearing: no cut renders without them. drawtext only writes the LABEL on a placeholder slate, and the assembler now renders an unlabelled slate and reports the degradation instead of failing the export. So drawtext must NOT block an install — the Linux ffmpeg-static build (7.0.2) lacks it while the macOS one (6.0) has it, and losing a caption on an unshot beat is not worth refusing a working studio.

provider._note: A REFERENCE, not a run spec. How to start this backend, the CUT LANE COMPANION that renders what its write verbs enqueue, and the byte routes it serves are declared by the provider itself in providers/studio-cutdown/provider.json. The companion mattered most: while it lived here, retiring this app would have taken the renderer with it and left the write verbs accepting work nothing performs — the same shape that cost this repo live rig state when the AGENTS app was retired.
